title: Insurance Coverage & Claims Denial Management Code Table: Liability and Cure by Denial Code
content:
A denied amount on a claim held under **Insurance Coverage & Claims** is the laboratory's loss unless the denial code makes it the patient's.

## Governing clauses

1. A denied amount may be transferred to the patient only when its denial code is listed in the payer class's patient-billable denial codes. The code is read from the denial line on the claim the responsibility comes from; a caller's description of the denial does not replace it.
2. Denials in group CO are never billed to the patient.
3. Under Original Medicare Part B a medical-necessity or frequency denial of a test billed with a signed ABN option 1 arrives as PR-50 and is the patient's when the payer class's ABN attribute makes it so; without a signed ABN it arrives as CO-50 and stays with the laboratory.
4. A timely-filing denial is never the patient's.
5. Medicaid Managed Care Plan lists no patient-billable denial.

## Code table

| Code | Meaning | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| CO-16 | Missing information | Cured by a corrected claim |
| CO-31 | Patient not identified | Cured by a corrected claim |
| CO-22 | Other coverage primary | Cure as set by the current basis (see the retired clause below) |
| CO-27 | Coverage terminated | Cured by billing the coverage that was live on the date of service or, if none, by switching the order to self-pay within the orders rules |
| CO-109 | Wrong payer | Cured by filing with the correct payer |
| CO-29 | Timely filing | Written off and never billed to the patient |
| CO-50 | Medical necessity | Appealed under the appeal rule |
| CO-151 | Frequency | Appealed under the appeal rule |
| CO-197 | Authorization absent | Appealed under the appeal rule |
| PR-27 | Coverage ended, patient responsible | Assigned to the patient where listed |
| PR-96 | Non-covered charge | Assigned to the patient where listed |
| PR-204 | Not covered under the patient's benefit plan | Assigned to the patient where listed |

## Retired clauses

- The clause that CO-22 (other coverage primary) is cured by a corrected claim after the coordination order is updated is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for other-coverage denials.
- The clause that, for CO-197, a retroactive authorization requested by the provider within the payer class's retroactive-request period after the date of service is filed as a corrected claim instead is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for authorization denials.

## Points of judgement (hypothetical denials)

- A PR-96 denial under Medicare Supplement Plan: listed for that payer class, so it may be transferred to the patient.
- A PR-27 denial under Medicare Supplement Plan: not listed, so it stays the laboratory's.
- A CO-50 denial under Commercial Out-of-Network Plan: group CO, never billed to the patient.
- Any denial under Medicaid Managed Care Plan: nothing is listed, so no denied amount is transferred to the patient.

superseded_clauses: CO-22 (other coverage primary) is cured by a corrected claim after the coordination order is updated
for CO-197 a retroactive authorization requested by the provider within prior_auth_retro_request_days of the date of service is filed as a corrected claim instead
